title: 2026-11-05_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_311
description: Investigate a compromised host infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' as the passkey.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' as the passkey.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. List all services to identify the suspicious one:
   ```
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or those that are not part of standard system services.
4. The suspicious service is likely to be named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match standard system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service might have a name that includes "kernel" or "service" but is not a standard system service.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. Check the status of the suspicious service identified in the previous task:
   ```
   systemctl status systemkernelservicedefender.service
   ```
3. Look for the port number in the service configuration. The port number is likely specified in the `ExecStart` line.
4. The port number used by the suspicious service is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status <service>` to check the status and configuration of the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number in the `ExecStart` line of the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is likely to be a standard port number, such as 80 or 443.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Timer
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
   ```
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. List all timers to identify the one responsible for periodic execution of the suspicious service:
   ```
   systemctl list-timers --all
   ```
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names. Pay attention to timers with unusual descriptions or those that are not part of standard system timers.
4. The suspicious timer is likely to be named `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions that do not match standard system timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious timer might have a name that includes "checkin" or "lab".
